payload.rebuttal:
argued: Under the notes' own patterns, a successful match can never end on a newline character, so match.end() and match.end() - 1 land text.count("
", 0, X) on the identical value for every match these patterns produce. Every place the regex consumes a newline mid-match (the `(?:
(?:[ 	]+\S|\)).*)*` continuation) requires consuming at least one more non-newline character in the same step before it can repeat or stop, and the opening `.*` and the triple-quote close `(?P=t)` end the same way, on a quote or paren or arbitrary text, never on `
` itself. I confirmed this by scanning every match the pattern produces over saffron's own source (59 matches) and found text[match.end()-1] == "
" in none of them, and by patching the line and rerunning the full constant-mutant and finish suites, which stayed green. The criterion requires the notes' pattern verbatim, so I cannot invent a different grammar just to manufacture a distinguishing case. match.end() - 1 is still the correct general expression and I have left it as is, but no test driven by the declared patterns can kill this specific wrong version, because it is not actually a different function under them.
